hero.alt: Green illustration with the title Does Swearing Break Wudu

sources.title: Quran 5:6 (Surah Al-Ma'idah), Quran.com
sources.supports: Commands wudu before prayer; Ibn Kathir excerpt says it is obligatory when impure and recommended when pure.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 225, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Prayer of one who has broken wudu is not accepted until he performs ablution.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 176, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Abu Hurairah explains hadath as passing wind; chapter limits repeating wudu to what exits the two passages.

sources.title: Passing Wind, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: States that anything exiting the front and back passage nullifies wudu.

sources.title: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1977, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: The believer does not insult honour, curse, or speak obscenely; graded hasan.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should talk what is good or keep quiet.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 4860, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Whoever swears by al-Lat and al-Uzza should say la ilaha illallah.

review.notes: Read each retrieved page text this run: Quran 5:6 with Ibn Kathir excerpt, Muslim 225, Bukhari 176, 4860, 6018, Tirmidhi 1977 and Darul Ifta Birmingham passing-wind fatwa. No source lists speech among nullifiers; article says swearing does not break wudu based on the physical nullifier evidence and frames renewal as optional per the Ibn Kathir excerpt. Muslim 244 returned 403 and was not used. Hero inspected: 1200x630 title card.

claim_checks.claim: Allah commands wudu before prayer and mentions relieving oneself
claim_checks.explanation: Verse text commands washing before prayer and names relieving oneself.

claim_checks.claim: Wudu before prayer is obligatory when impure and recommended when pure
claim_checks.explanation: Ibn Kathir excerpt on the page states exactly this distinction.

claim_checks.claim: Prayer not accepted after breaking wudu until ablution
Hadath explained as passing wind; chapter about two passages
claim_checks.explanation: Narration and chapter heading on the page match.

claim_checks.claim: What exits the front and back passages nullifies wudu
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa states anything exiting the front and back passage nullifies wudu.

claim_checks.claim: Believer does not curse or speak obscenely; hasan
claim_checks.explanation: Tirmidhi 1977 text and Darussalam hasan grade on page.

claim_checks.claim: Oath by al-Lat and al-Uzza remedied by saying la ilaha illallah, no wudu mentioned
claim_checks.explanation: Bukhari 4860 prescribes saying la ilaha illallah and does not mention ablution.
